## Scope

All records are synthetic. This report demonstrates the first milestone of an
independent portfolio project. CP is implemented in a separate module; CRC remains planned.
The endpoint and assumed effect are hypothetical, with no clinical validation.

## Trial design

There are 240 patients, randomized equally to investigational treatment or control.
The primary endpoint is improvement at week 12; larger values are favorable.
The intended treatment-policy estimand is the mean randomized-arm difference.
The initial simulation contains no intercurrent events or missing measurements.

## Sample-size illustration

```{r}
knitr::kable(read.csv("outputs/sample_size_planning.csv"), digits = 3)
```

This normal approximation ignores covariate-adjustment gains and has no dropout
allowance. It is a planning illustration, not a clinical recommendation.

## Baseline characteristics

```{r}
knitr::kable(read.csv("outputs/baseline_table.csv"), digits = 2)
```

## Primary efficacy analysis

```{r}
knitr::kable(read.csv("outputs/efficacy_results.csv"), digits = 4)
```

The treatment coefficient comes from ANCOVA adjusted for baseline score, age,
and biomarker. Its confidence interval concerns a mean treatment effect.
It is not an individual-patient prediction interval.

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("outputs/efficacy_plot.png")
```

## Descriptive safety

```{r}
knitr::kable(read.csv("outputs/safety_table.csv"), digits = 1)
```

Events are binary occurrences during follow-up; recurrence and severity are not
represented. These tables do not establish the safety of a real treatment.

## Repeated simulation

```{r}
knitr::kable(read.csv("outputs/operating_characteristics.csv"), digits = 4)
```

Rejection under the null estimates Type I error; rejection under the alternative
estimates power. Monte Carlo standard errors and intervals quantify simulation
precision, distinct from confidence intervals for a trial's treatment effect.

## Next milestone

Review the separate arm-specific split conformal experiment, then implement
adverse-event prediction sets calibrated with CRC. Assess coverage,
width, expected missed-event fraction, and alert burden. Preserve the distinction
between these predictive objectives and the trial's efficacy test.
